Retroactive LaTeX-converter bugfix found during stage 10's own PDF page-render spot check (a rendered page of ex_3.1's Table 3.1 header showed literal, visible '</sub>' tag text leaking onto the page - e.g. '[C4</sub> H9</sub> Cl]t2</sub></sub>'). Root cause: latex_convert.py's \left/\right handler tried to detect an escaped literal brace delimiter (\left\{ / \right\}, used in ex_3.1's Table 3.1 header - a \begin{aligned} cell wrapping nested chemical-formula subscripts in \left\{...\right\}) via a regex requiring a LETTER immediately after the backslash (\\[a-zA-Z]+) - which never matches a non-letter escape like '\{', so the two branches meant to convert it to a literal brace character were unreachable dead code. The backslash got consumed alone, leaving the bare '{' character unconsumed, which the NEXT loop iteration swept into the generic brace-group reader (`if c == "{": inner = _read_group(p); buf.append(_convert(inner))`) - reading the ENTIRE \left\{...\right\} span (including its own nested \frac/sub/sup content) as one group, recursively converting it to HTML, and dropping that already-tag-wrapped HTML straight into the plain-text buffer. When that buffer was later padded by _finish_plain_text()'s operator-spacing regex (which pads a bare '/' with non-breaking spaces), it matched the '/' INSIDE the nested content's own '</sub>' closing tags and corrupted them into '<\xa0/\xa0sub>' - exactly the general failure mode the module's own docstring already documents ('never let tag-producing HTML enter buf'), resurfacing via this specific escaped-brace path. Fixed by matching '\{'/'\}' as an explicit 2-character token check before falling back to the general \\[a-zA-Z]+ regex, so the literal brace is fully consumed as its own ordinary buffered character and never reaches the group-reading branch at all. Confirmed this pattern (\left\{) appears exactly once in this chapter (ex_3.1's Table 3.1 header) and zero times in chemistry-12-1/chemistry-12-2's own 06_simplify sources (grep-confirmed) - rebuilt both chapters' pages after this fix as a precaution and confirmed their final.en.html came out byte-identical (md5 unchanged), so no re-export was needed for either. Re-ran chemistry-12-3's own full chain after the fix: stage 8 JSON regenerated (unaffected, gates pass), 09_design/final.en.html rebuilt (195,408 bytes), numeric read-back re-run (116 fields, 0 missing), visually re-confirmed the fixed table renders correctly with clean nested subscripts and no stray tag text.
